simple.meaning: חֵמֶת (chêmeth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a skin bottle (as tied up).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 21:14. The surrounding context includes wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֵמֶת (H2573) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: חֵמֶת (chêmeth) / H2573 is traced through Genesis 21:14, Genesis 21:15, Genesis 21:19, Habakkuk 2:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a container of water, and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder; and gave her the child, and sent her away. She departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.

timeline.evidenceText: Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a container of water, and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder; and gave her the child, and sent her away. She departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
The water in the container was spent, and she put the child under one of the shrubs.
God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went, filled the container with water, and gave the boy a drink.
“Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink, pouring your inflaming wine until they are drunk, so that you may gaze at their naked bodies!
